subject: Urgent: peak-hour SSE p99 regressions affecting BrightChat production
messages:
From: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@brightchat.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightChat SRE Team <sre@brightchat.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes on SSE during 08:00-09:30 PST window

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing severe tail-latency regressions on the streaming chat endpoint (SSE) this morning during our peak. p95 is fine, but p99 shot up to ~8.2s for user-facing messages between 08:10-09:25 PST. This correlates with a backlog of open connections and a handful of 503s.

Attached are a short set of traces and a screenshot of our dashboard (sse-traces-05-23-2028.zip / brightchat-tail-screenshots-05-23.png). We're already routing non-critical traffic to the fallback model but the latency hit is driving customer complaints.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a capacity/queueing issue or a regression from the recent runtime change you rolled last week? Need an ETA and any mitigation we can apply on our side.

—Sofia
Sofia Delgado
Head of Platform Reliability, BrightChat

- Michael — please evaluate whether last week's runtime change (kernel selection fallback) could cause pathologically long single-request latencies under high concurrent prefix-share.

I'm putting this on Sean's radar for exec attention if we need credits/SLA exceptions.

Date: 2028-05-23T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 spikes on SSE during 08:00-09:30 PST window

Jasmine / team — quick findings from initial triage:

- Observed the same spike in our hosted API telemetry for the BrightChat tenant: concurrent open SSE connections rose ~35% compared to baseline for that window.
- The SSE worker pool hit a long-tail eviction path where requests with large prefix-KV cache misses fell back to the slower kernel. This increases single-request latency asymmetrically, spiking p99 while leaving p95 relatively stable.
- Autoscaler did add nodes but there was a short period (~4m) where the request queue depth exceeded our soft-scaling threshold, which amplified head-of-line queueing for connections on the slower kernel.

Immediate mitigations I recommend we push (fast):
1) Apply an emergency runtime flag to prefer hot kernels for SSE connections for this customer (reduces worst-case path).
2) Temporarily raise the soft-scaling threshold and trigger a rapid scale-up policy for their pool.
3) Ask BrightChat to enable per-tenant prefix-caching for high-frequency chat channels (they can toggle in the Console; quick doc link below).

I'll open INF-7892 and attach the traces; pushing a quick patch to the canary fleet now for kernel preference. ETA for patch rollout ~25 minutes.

—Karthik
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@brightchat.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, michael_grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T10:31:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 spikes on SSE during 08:00-09:30 PST window

Sofia — thanks for the traces and patience. We appreciate the detail; this helped pinpoint the kernel-fallback pattern.

Immediate steps we've taken:
- Enabled a kernel-preference flag for your tenant's SSE pool (applied to canary then rolled to your pool at 10:20 PST).
- Raised soft-scaling aggressiveness for the next 2 hours.
- Sent a configuration toggle for per-tenant prefix-caching you can enable now if you want (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_playbook).

We expect a measurable improvement within one customer peak cycle. If you still see >2s p99 after one hour, please let me know and we'll open a deeper dive with an on-call from the serving kernel team.

Apologies for the interruption — we will follow up with a post-mortem and a draft of a customer-facing incident note.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RE: Sudden p99 spikes on SSE during 08:00-09:30 PST window

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few notes for the exec channel and next actions:

- Customer impact was limited to tail latency and a small fraction of requests 503ing; no data loss. BrightChat saw reduced complaint volume after the kernel preference and scale changes.
- We should draft a short executive summary for BrightChat's leadership that includes: timeline, root cause (kernel fallback + transient autoscaling gap), mitigations applied, and proposed SLAs/credits if requested. Jasmine, please prepare the external note and cc: me.
- Karthik / Michael: schedule a follow-up to harden the kernel-selection fallback path so a single-request slower path cannot dominate p99 under moderate concurrency. Consider adding a per-tenant circuit-breaker for fallback invocation.
- Marissa: post-mortem and customer incident note; include suggested console defaults for high-concurrency SSE tenants (prefix-caching enabled).

I'll hold off on public exec escalation unless BrightChat requests account-level credits or broader SLA conversation. Good work.

—Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
